micro_class_error_analysis: The worst-performing macro-class was 'WATER' (F1 = 0.7858). Cross-tabulation of the 113 misclassified test samples reveals the following patterns: 'wetland' was most frequently misclassified as GREENERY (20 times) because wetlands contain dense vegetation that dominates the spectral signature at 64x64 resolution, making them visually indistinguishable from pure greenery. 'ship' was predicted as CEMENT_INFRASTRUCTURE (23 times) because ships appear as grey rectangular structures against the water background, sharing texture with roads and buildings. 'snowberg' was predicted as CEMENT_INFRASTRUCTURE (10 times) because white and grey ice patches closely resemble concrete surfaces at coarse resolution. 'river' was predicted as CEMENT_INFRASTRUCTURE (8 times) because narrow rivers flanked by urban banks are easily confused with roads or grey infrastructure. These confusions are driven by three factors: (1) the 64x64 resolution loses fine structural cues that distinguish water from similar-textured surfaces, (2) WATER is a spectrally diverse macro-class combining open water, ice, ships, and wetlands which have very different appearances, and (3) the weighted loss partially mitigated but did not fully resolve these cross-class ambiguities. Mitigation strategies include higher input resolution (128x128), separating ship/snowberg into their own class, and using attention mechanisms to focus on discriminative water-specific features.
